texts.preamble: Sunilkumar Vinodbhai Shah vs C S Gohil on 10 August, 2017 Author: Vipul M. Pancholi Bench: Vipul M. Pancholi R/Cr.Ma/4599/2009 Judgment In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad Criminal Misc.Application No. 4599 of 2009 For Approval And Signature: Honourable Mr.Justice Vipul M. Pancholi ========================================================== 1
texts.facts: By way of this application which is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as `the Code' for short), the applicant seeks quashing of the criminal complaint bearing no.27464 of 2008 for the offences punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as `the PFA Act' for short) filed by respondent no.1 pending in the court of learned J.M.F.C.,Surat.
texts.arguments: 2. Learned advocate Mr.Manan Shah for the applicant submitted that he has received instructions to appear on behalf of the applicant and he will file vakalatnama within a period of three days from today. Learned advocate Mr.Shah for the applicant submits that the impugned complaint came to be filed against the applicant and others under the provisions of the PFA Act alleging the violation of the provisions of the said Act. It is alleged in the said complaint that the present applicant is working as a Manager of the firm namely Shri Ronak Beverages and Food P.Ltd. It is alleged that sample of packaged drinking water was taken on 27.3.2008 and after following the HC-NIC Page 2 of 12 Created On Mon Aug 21 11:32:22 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/4599/2009 JUDGMENT procedure prescribed under the said Act, sample was sent to the local laboratory for necessary analysis. The concerned Laboratory submitted the report on 5.5.2008 in which the concerned public analyst gave his opinion that the sample of packaged drinking water is adulterated as it does not comply with the microbiological standards laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulterated Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as `PFA Rules' for short) in respect of aerobic microbial counts. Similarly, for another sample, similar opinion was given by the concerned public analyst. It is contended that though the shelf life of the product in question was upto 26.9.2008, the impugned complaint came to be filed on 20.10.2008. It is, therefore, submitted that the impugned complaint is filed after the shelf life of the drinking water in question has expired. Thus, it is submitted that the applicant-accused could not request to the trial Court for sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory and therefore he lost the opportunity for sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory. Hence, prejudice is caused to the applicant-accused. It is further alleged that the complainant has thereby violated the mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the PFA Act. Learned advocate for the applicant, therefore, requested that the impugned complaint be [LEAKAGE_MASK] HC-NIC Page 3 of 12 Created On Mon Aug 21 11:32:22 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/4599/2009 JUDGMENT and [LEAKAGE_MASK] only on this ground. 4. Learned advocate Mr.Shah appearing for the applicant has placed reliance upon the order dated 1.2.2016 passed by this Court in Criminal Revision Application No.475 of 2011 in the case of State of Gujarat V/s Nareshkumar Gordhandas Hotvani in support of his contention. Learned advocate submitted that the present case is squarely covered by the aforesaid decision and therefore the impugned complaint be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Sunilkumar Vinodbhai Shah vs C S Gohil on 10 August, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62671749/ 2 5. On the other hand, learned APP Mr.Devnani for the respondent-State is not in a position to deny the factual aspect that the impugned complaint is filed on 20.10.2008 before which the shelf life of the drinking water in question has expired on 26.9.2008. Learned APP Mr.Devnani has fairly submitted that the decision upon which the reliance is placed by the learned advocate for the applicant is applicable to the facts of the present case. 6. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the parties and having gone through the material produced on record and the decision upon which the reliance is placed by the learned advocate for the applicant, it has emerged that HC-NIC Page 4 of 12 Created On Mon Aug 21 11:32:22 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/4599/2009 JUDGMENT the sample of the packaged drinking water was taken by the Food Inspector on 27.3.2008 and after following due procedure, the same was sent for necessary analysis to the local laboratory situated at Vadodara. , the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the person from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an Sunilkumar Vinodbhai Shah vs C S Gohil (2A) When an application is made to the Court under subsection (2), the Court shall require the Local (Health) Authority to forward the part or parts of the sample kept by the said Authority and upon such requisition being made, the said Authority shall forward the part or parts of the sample to the Court within a period of five days from the date of receipt of such requisition. (2B) On receipt of the part or parts of the sample from the Local (Health) Authority under subsection (2A), the Court shall first ascertain that the mark and seal or fastening as provided in clause (b) of subsection (1) of section 11 are intact and the signature or thumb impression, as the case may be, is not tampered with, and dispatch the part or, as the case may be, one of the parts of the sample under its own seal to the Director of the Central Food Laboratory who shall thereupon send a certificate to the Court in the prescribed form within one month from the date of receipt of the part of the sample specifying the result of the analysis. HC-NIC Page 7 of 12 Created On Mon Aug 21 11:32:22 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/4599/2009 JUDGMENT (2C) Where two parts of the sample have been sent to the Court and of one part of the sample has been sent by the Court to the Director of the Central Food Laboratory under subsection (2B) the Court shall, as soon as practicable, return the remaining part to the Local (Health) Authority and that Authority shall destroy that part after the certificate from the Director of the Central Food Laboratory has been received by the Court : Provided that where the part of the sample sent by the Court to the Director of the Central Food Laboratory is lost or damaged, the Court shall require the Local (Health) Authority to forward the part of the sample, if any, retained by it to the Court and on receipt thereof, the Court shall proceed in the manner provided in subsection (2B). (2D) Until the receipt of the certificate of the result of the analysis from the Director of the Central Food Laboratory, the Court shall not continue with the proceedings pending before it in relation to the prosecution. In the case of Nareshkumar Gordhandas HC-NIC Page 8 of 12 Created On Mon Aug 21 11:32:22 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/4599/2009 JUDGMENT Hotvani(supra), this Court, after referring to the similar provisions contained in Section 24 of the Insecticides Act of 1963 as well as Section 25 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act of 1940 and also after considering the decisions rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Medicamen Biotech Limited V/s Rubina Bose, Drug Inspector, reported in (2008)7 SCC 196 and another decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana V/s Unique Farmaid P.Limited and others reported in 1992(2) FAC 399 observed in paragraph 10, 11 and 14 as under: "10. 11. In the case of M/s. Medicamen Biotech Limited (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed in paragraph No.10 as under: "10.
